summary.text: In an interview published December 16, 2025, Warsh, identified as a former Federal Reserve governor, described AI as an exciting opportunity for U.S. prosperity and a stronger workforce. In his July 14, 2026 testimony as chairman, Warsh acknowledged uncertainty about the benefits of the AI buildout and said the Fed was monitoring implications for inflation and the labor market. On August 28, 2026, he linked AI progress to the potential for substantially higher growth while raising questions about productivity, labor, and capital requirements.

statements.text: We recognize that AI is a new variable—potentially a new factor of production—that will have consequences for both the economy and the conduct of monetary policy. It opens some major lines of inquiry: Will the application of AI cause a significant, sustained rise in productivity across the economy? And if so, when? Will token usage be complementary or competitive to labor? Will the next generation of AI models demand even greater capital intensity, or will the models themselves help devise a capital-light solution?
